Joining loans to readable labels

Unit 2 · Week 5 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open a fresh working copy of database-project.sqlite in a school-approved SQLite tool. Keep sql-starter.sqlite unchanged. The project edition adds Equipment.ReplacementCost. Review database-project-setup.sql and use database-project-workbook.md, database-project-answers.md and database-project-reports.sql. Use fictional data and public explained answers. No cloud account is required. These 55-minute timings are flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Joining loans to readable labels

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the separate database-project.sqlite edition of the equipment desk. ReplacementCost contains fictional whole-dollar teaching estimates, not current prices. Activities are ungraded. This week practices joins and summaries; controlled changes follow in Week 6. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

2. A report needs facts from several tables

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and prediction

Recall that each Loan row is one borrowing event. BorrowerID and EquipmentID are FKs. The result should show readable labels without copying them into stored Loan rows. Introduce the separate project database and its cost field; retain four Borrower, three Category, five Equipment and six Loan rows. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

3. One loan, two key matches

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

Trace L001 by hand before showing SQL. The ON conditions must match corresponding identifiers. EquipmentDescription is unsuitable for identifying a physical item because E01 and E04 are both Camera. A join creates a query result without merging the stored tables. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

4. A readable active-loan query

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with predictions

An alias qualifies the source of a field: l.BorrowerID belongs to Loan labelled l. INNER JOIN keeps matching rows. ON supplies the key match. The four active events are L001, L006, L002, L004 in due-date order. DueDate can determine ordering without appearing in this selected result. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

5. The complete active-loan result

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

These are four event rows, not a count of distinct descriptions. L001 and L004 have different item/borrower keys even though their descriptions match. The query reads l.DueDate for ordering. Compare all returned rows with the source records, not just the row count. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

6. A join to explain independently

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook question 1 for the key trace. L002 links to B002 Learner B and E02 Tripod, with due date 2026-04-08 and Returned=0. Learners should name both source and target fields. Optional support: follow L001 again, then explain L002 without the model. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

7. The tables stay separate

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. The DBMS matches Loan.BorrowerID to Borrower.BorrowerID and reads BorrowerLabel for the result. The stored relational structure remains separate. Later changing a label changes the managed borrower fact rather than every loan event. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

8. A new loan, an existing borrower

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

A distinct LoanID identifies the new event. BorrowerID can repeat across Loan rows, as can EquipmentID across history. A new current loan still needs valid references and a separate availability/overlap check. Do not remove legitimate repeated references. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.
